rationale: Checked the DRfold2 repository today: it does ship reusable artifacts - the install script states "This will download model weights ~1.3GB and install Arena.", and the repository licence is MIT-form text (Copyright (c) 2025 Yang Li). No direct weight URL is exposed in the README (download is via install.sh), so the artifact locator is indirect. Both remaining paths are curatorial acts the register must perform, not facts an external page can settle.

name: FrameDiff / FrameFlow / Multiflow
condition: Split FrameDiff, FrameFlow and MultiFlow into independently evidenced records, or narrow this record to a single system.
licence_quote: MultiFlow repo licence as shown today: "LICENSE: MIT". FrameFlow repo licence as shown today: "MIT license".
rationale: Fetched both cited repositories today. github.com/jasonkyuyim/multiflow implements MultiFlow only ("We provide pre-trained model weights at this Zenodo link", weights.tar.gz; MIT); github.com/microsoft/frame-flow is live, not archived, implements FrameFlow ("Datasets and weights are hosted on Zenodo", weights.tar.gz ~0.6 GB; MIT) and notes only a legacy branch for the older workshop-paper version. So the three systems remain distinct upstream projects with separate repos and separate weight bundles, which is exactly why the merged record is held. The condition is an editorial split/narrowing that the register has not performed - no external evidence can satisfy it. No sign of rename, absorption or withdrawal, so no update_note.

name: ProtGPS
condition: Reconsider if broader reusable foundation-model scope is established by primary evidence, or if a written task-specific exception is adopted.
licence_quote: Repository licence label shown today: "MIT license".
rationale: Fetched the official repository today. Artifacts are fine - MIT licence, code plus notebooks, and checkpoints released off-repo ("Download model checkpoints from zenodo and extract to checkpoints/protgps"), with ESM2 and DR-BERT weights pulled from Torch Hub/HuggingFace. But the hold is about scope, and the repository still presents a single localization objective (paper framing: "Protein codes promote selective subcellular compartmentalization"), i.e. 12-compartment prediction plus localization-conditioned generation. No broader reusable pretraining is evidenced, and no written task-specific exception exists in the catalog repo (Foundation_models/CHANGELOG.md stops at 2026-07-14 and contains no policy change). Condition unmet on both branches.
